shots.line: The teacher is still reading the instructions.
shots.scene: Establishing wide of a morning classroom: TEACHER at the board reading a sheet, four black background kids at desks, LEON in the front row, window light from the left, slow push

shots.line: Sixty minutes, no calculators, do not turn the page until I say start.
shots.scene: Medium on TEACHER reading, chalk board plates behind her with kText '60 MINUTES' then 'NO CALCULATORS' as spoken; a kid yawns in the blur foreground

shots.line: You turn the page.
shots.scene: Insert: LEON's hand turning the page, dust motes in the window beam

shots.line: By the time she looks up, the test is finished, all fifty questions, and your pencil is back behind your ear.
shots.scene: Medium two-shot: LEON with the finished test (check marks, card '50 / 50' pops in), pencil behind his ear, TEACHER lifting her eyes in the back; ear-pencil gesture

shots.line: "Leon, I haven't said start." "Yeah. I'm just waiting for the others."
shots.scene: Over-the-shoulder two-shot: TEACHER (talk) 'Leon, I haven't said start.' then LEON (talk, smirk) 'Yeah. I'm just waiting for the others.'; quoted lines appear as bubbles

shots.line: Somebody in the back drops an eraser.
shots.scene: Wide: back of the room, a black kid's eraser drops and bounces on the floor, everyone freezes, camera drifts toward LEON

shots.line: And that was the easy part.
shots.scene: Giant face close-up of LEON, smirk, looks at camera, slow push; class gape behind in blur

shots.line: So, what if you had an IQ of nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine?
shots.scene: Title card over a glowing wide: LEON centre, golden glow, caps title 'WHAT IF YOU HAD AN IQ OF 9,999?' with kText slam on the number

shots.line: Quick reality check first.
shots.scene: Insert: a blueprint IQ scale as a ruler, camera starts at 0

shots.line: Real tests stop at around one hundred and sixty, because nobody above that has ever been measured well.
shots.scene: Blueprint ruler runs to a mark '160' near the right end, then empty grid; labels 'REAL TESTS STOP AT ≈160' and 'NEVER MEASURED WELL ABOVE'

shots.line: So your number doesn't just beat the scale, it breaks it. That's the fun part. Here's how it works. Rule one.
shots.scene: The ruler snaps in half, pieces fly, gold number '9,999' drops through and cracks the grid; LEON stands on a shard in the foreground; end with caption 'HERE'S HOW IT WORKS'

shots.line: IQ isn't a pile of points, it's a rank.
shots.scene: Plate RULE 1: big '1', a pile of coin icons crossed out, arrow to a staircase; labels 'IQ = RANK, NOT POINTS'

shots.line: The average person gets one hundred, and every fifteen points is one step up.
shots.scene: Staircase from below: base step with an average stickman, labels '100 = AVERAGE' and '+15 = 1 STEP'; camera climbs step by step

shots.line: Even a genius at one hundred and sixty is only four steps above average.
shots.scene: Same staircase: a genius with glasses on step 4, steps 1-4 highlight in gold, label '160 = 4 STEPS UP'

shots.line: You're about six hundred and sixty steps up.
shots.scene: Pull-out up: the staircase continues into clouds, LEON at the very top beside the moon, label '≈660 STEPS UP' in gold, crowd tiny below

shots.line: You're not winning the race, you're in a different sport. Rule two.
shots.scene: Split: stadium with ink runners on the left track, LEON on the stands with a chess board on the right; then plate RULE 2 slides in

shots.line: Your head is the same size.
shots.scene: Two identical head profiles side by side with matching size arrows, label 'SAME SIZE HEAD'

shots.line: Same brain, same fuel, a fifth of your body's energy, from the same sandwiches.
shots.scene: Brain cut-away with a meter, one fifth filled in gold, label '1/5 OF BODY'S ENERGY', a sandwich icon underneath

shots.line: You didn't get a bigger battery, you got a much better program.
shots.scene: Left: big battery with a red cross; right: a screen with neat program lines and a check; LEON points to the screen, quick cut between them

shots.line: Rule three.
shots.scene: Plate RULE 3: lightning bolt over LEON's head, snail at his feet

shots.line: You think instantly, but your body doesn't.
shots.scene: LEON stands still, thought bolt above, body in slow motion (ghost trail lagging), label 'MIND: INSTANT · BODY: SLOW'

shots.line: Same hands, same legs, same nerves,
shots.scene: Nerve diagram: head to hand along a line, a spark starts to run

shots.line: and a nerve signal tops out around four hundred kilometres an hour, about two hundred and fifty miles an hour. Fast for a body.
shots.scene: Spark races along the nerve, speedometer needle hits the limit, readouts '≈400 KM/H' and '≈250 MPH' pop in as spoken

shots.line: Slow for you. And one limit.
shots.scene: Speedometer beside a jet, then LEON tapping a watch; end on his raised finger, label 'ONE LIMIT'

shots.line: You can't know what you've never seen.
shots.scene: LEON before a closed door with light leaking under it, slow push, unsure

shots.line: You can work out almost anything from almost nothing, but you're a mind, not a search engine.
shots.scene: From a single paw print LEON draws a whole deduction diagram; a magnifier icon crossed out

shots.line: Ask you about a country you've never heard of, and you'll guess its capital from the climate and the shape of the map. You'll probably be right.
shots.scene: Map of an unnamed country, LEON puts a dot by a river and a gold question mark grows over it

shots.line: But it's still a guess. Plus.
shots.scene: Label 'GUESS ≠ KNOW' then a hard cut to plate PLUS

shots.line: Homework takes nine seconds, and six of those are you looking for a pencil.
shots.scene: Medium: LEON at a desk with a finished notebook, patting his pockets for a pencil, a timer '9 SEC' counting down beside him

shots.line: Plus, you finish the teacher's sentences.
shots.scene: Two-shot: TEACHER with a long sentence in a bubble, LEON's bubble finishing it, label PLUS

shots.line: Not the short ones, the long ones, the ones with three commas.
shots.scene: Insert: the teacher's bubble with three commas highlighted, LEON rolls his eyes

shots.line: Plus, Saturday at the grocery store.
shots.scene: Top-down wide of a grocery store: crowd dots, label PLUS, camera pushes toward the entrance

shots.line: You look at the crowd once, and you see the shortest path through it,
shots.scene: Top-down: LEON draws a glowing shortest path through the crowd dots

shots.line: the checkout line that will actually move, and the guy who's about to turn his cart without looking. You're out in three minutes.
shots.scene: Top-down: the path reaches a moving checkout line, a man with a cart turns without looking (coral arrow), LEON slides past

shots.line: Mom is still looking for a parking spot. Plus, languages.
shots.scene: Golden hour: LEON waits by the exit with a bag, MOM's car circling the lot in the background; card '3 MIN'; then cut to plate PLUS

shots.line: You learn Spanish on the bus, and by the third stop you're correcting the driver's grammar.
shots.scene: Inside a bus: LEON with a phrasebook, driver in the mirror, route line with three stops lighting up, label 'STOP 3'

shots.line: Plus, checkers with Grandpa.
shots.scene: Interior warm: GRANDPA and LEON at a checkers table by the window, calendar of Sundays on the wall, label PLUS

shots.line: Every Sunday for years, and he's never lost.
shots.scene: Close on the checkers board, GRANDPA smiling confidently, slow push

shots.line: Until you win in six moves.
shots.scene: Insert: LEON's move, board cleared, GRANDPA shocked; card '6 MOVES'

shots.line: Then you let him win the next game, because you're not a monster. He knows.
shots.scene: Two-shot: LEON deliberately leaves a checker hanging and winks; GRANDPA wins and laughs; cut to GRANDPA's wink back

shots.line: He pats your head and says, "You're getting better." Best Sunday ever.
shots.scene: Warm medium: GRANDPA pats LEON's cap, bubble 'You're getting better.', LEON squints happily; golden light

shots.line: So far, nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine looks amazing.
shots.scene: LEON in a golden glow with stars, big gold '9,999' behind, label '9,999 = AMAZING'

shots.line: But then you start noticing the problems. Problem one. You're hungry. All the time.
shots.scene: Glow drains to cold dark, question marks grow behind LEON; plate PROBLEM 1, label 'HUNGRY', stomach rumble

shots.line: Your brain is two percent of your weight and already burns a fifth of your energy,
shots.scene: Silhouette of LEON, head small, pie chart beside: 2% slice and a big 1/5 slice, labels '2% OF WEIGHT' and '1/5 OF ENERGY'

shots.line: and yours is working harder than any brain ever has.
shots.scene: The pie fills further, LEON's brain glows red, label 'HARDER THAN ANY BRAIN'

shots.line: A normal brain barely spends more when it thinks hard, usually under five percent. Yours would.
shots.scene: Two bars: normal brain small rise ('UNDER 5%'), LEON's bar breaks through the frame top

shots.line: So at ten fifteen, you're thinking about lunch.
shots.scene: Wall clock '10:15', LEON slumped at his desk eyeing a lunch bag; label 10:15

shots.line: At ten forty, you're thinking about a sandwich in extremely high resolution.
shots.scene: Wall clock '10:40', thought bubble with a huge sandwich; label 10:40, then the sandwich turns pixel-grid sharp

shots.line: You can calculate its exact calories, and it doesn't help.
shots.scene: LEON calculating, thought bubble with sandwich plus a calorie grid; he sighs and slumps

shots.line: You even design a better lunch tray, with a built-in cup holder and a snack drawer. Nobody asked.
shots.scene: Blueprint of a lunch tray with a cup holder and snack drawer in LEON's hands, classmates turn away

shots.line: In the cafeteria, you eat your lunch, then your friend's lunch, then you stare at the lunch lady's apple. "Leon, are you okay?"
shots.scene: Cafeteria wide: LEON eating, empty trays stacked, FRIEND horrified, LUNCHLADY with an apple, LEON staring at the apple; bubble 'Leon, are you okay?'

shots.line: "I'm thinking."
shots.scene: Close-up LEON (talk): 'I'm thinking.' eyes on the apple

shots.line: "You look like you're going to eat my tray." The fix is boring.
shots.scene: FRIEND with a tray (talk): 'You look like you're going to eat my tray.' LEON leaning in

shots.line: You carry food everywhere.
shots.scene: Plate THE FIX; LEON points to a pocket

shots.line: Peanuts in your pocket, a banana under your cap, a granola bar behind your ear.
shots.scene: Medium on LEON: peanuts in the pocket pop in (pop SFX)

shots.line: You're a walking snack bar, and you're not ashamed. Problem two. Your body is late.
shots.scene: Peanuts, a banana under the cap, a granola bar behind the ear; LEON proud; label 'WALKING SNACK BAR'

shots.line: A cup rolls off the table.
shots.scene: Plate PROBLEM 2: LEON and his shadow lagging behind; cut to table, a cup rolling off the edge, slow motion

shots.line: In your head, it already happened.
shots.scene: Macro: the falling cup with a dotted trajectory drawn ahead of it

shots.line: You know the speed, the angle, the exact spot where it lands, and you've planned seventeen ways to catch it.
shots.scene: LEON's head with 17 arrow paths radiating; label '17 WAYS'

shots.line: Your hand arrives when the cup is already in pieces.
shots.scene: Insert: LEON's hand arriving at pieces of the cup on the floor

shots.line: Four hundred kilometres an hour sounds fast, until your thoughts are faster.
shots.scene: Speedometer 400 KM/H being overtaken by a thought bolt

shots.line: So you're the smartest kid alive, and you're the clumsiest one in gym class.
shots.scene: Gym wide: ball in the air, LEON standing still with a calculation diagram over his head, kids waiting

shots.line: You know exactly where the ball will land, and you're still standing there when it hits your shoe. "Leon, move!"
shots.scene: Ball hits LEON's shoe with a thud; shot ends on a freeze with dust

shots.line: "I'm calculating!" "It's a ball!"
shots.scene: Medium: kids shouting 'Leon, move!', LEON, finger raised, 'I'm calculating!', a kid 'It's a ball!'

shots.line: The fix is planning ahead.
shots.scene: Plate THE FIX: PLAN AHEAD

shots.line: You can't react faster, so you decide earlier.
shots.scene: LEON reaches with an extended hand before the cup moves

shots.line: You start moving before the cup falls. Sometimes it looks like magic.
shots.scene: Close: LEON's hand under a cup that stands still; people behind in confusion

shots.line: Sometimes you're just holding a hand under a cup nobody dropped.
shots.scene: Pause gag: the hand under the unmoved cup, LEON smiles, everyone stares

shots.line: Last week you invented a better way to tie your shoes. In theory.
shots.scene: LEON with a diagram of a new shoe-tying method pinned on the wall; label 'IN THEORY'

shots.line: In practice, you're still wearing them on the wrong feet. Problem three. Sleep.
shots.scene: Close: LEON's sneakers on the wrong feet, one toe pointing inward; cut to plate PROBLEM 3

shots.line: And this one is bigger than the others, so stay with me. You find a problem.
shots.scene: Plate PROBLEM 3: huge moon and pillow, label 'SLEEP'; LEON at a window

shots.line: Not a school one, a real one,
shots.scene: LEON at a desk under a lamp, notebook with famous problem scribbles, determined face

shots.line: a famous math problem nobody has solved in a hundred years, and you can feel the answer is close.
shots.scene: Blackboard filled with a huge unreadable formula, glow, label '100 YEARS', slow push

shots.line: So you skip bedtime.
shots.scene: LEON waves away the bed (empty, made) in the background, determined

shots.line: Why waste eight hours when your brain works this fast? Midnight. Two in the morning. Four. You're so close.
shots.scene: Clock sequence 12:00 AM, 2:00 AM, 4:00 AM, LEON getting messier, paper stacks growing

shots.line: At three, you write a proof that looks beautiful.
shots.scene: Close: a page with a beautiful proof, LEON beaming

shots.line: At five, you notice the first line says two plus two is five. Here's what you don't know.
shots.scene: Insert: the first line of the proof says '2 + 2 = 5', a red circle drawn around it; LEON's face drops

shots.line: Sleep isn't a pause. Your brain is cleaning.
shots.scene: Blueprint brain-room: tiny stick cleaners with buckets wash the brain; label 'SLEEP = CLEANING'

shots.line: In a study from twenty thirteen in the journal Science, on mice,
shots.scene: Sleeping mouse; label 'SCIENCE, 2013 (MICE)'

shots.line: researchers measured that the space between brain cells opens up by about sixty percent during sleep,
shots.scene: Cell diagram: gaps between cells widen, label '+60% SPACE'

shots.line: and that lets the brain wash out waste, including a protein linked to Alzheimer's.
shots.scene: Waste washes out in a stream, label 'WASTE WASHED OUT'

shots.line: Sleep is also when new memories get locked in.
shots.scene: Brain close-up, memories as small boxes being locked in

shots.line: In people, when you skip it, the memory centre, the hippocampus,
shots.scene: Hippocampus lights up (seahorse shape), label 'HIPPOCAMPUS'

shots.line: works worse at saving new things, even when you try hard to stay alert.
shots.scene: A brain with tired eyes; a save icon fails; LEON with wide-open eyes in the corner

shots.line: So at six in the morning, your genius brain has the answer on a napkin, and you can't read your own handwriting.
shots.scene: Morning at the desk, LEON holding a napkin with scribbles, pale light; label 6:00 AM, he squints

shots.line: At seven, roll call. "Leon?" You open your mouth. Nothing. Not "here". Not your name. Nothing.
shots.scene: Roll call: TEACHER with a register, LEON with his mouth open, nothing; label 7:00 AM; quote 'Leon?'

shots.line: "Leon?"
shots.scene: Close: TEACHER (talk): 'Leon?' LEON blank

shots.line: The kid next to you whispers, "That's you." "Is it?" That's the problem.
shots.scene: Two-shot: KID whispering 'That's you.' LEON 'Is it?' confused

shots.line: The fastest brain in the world, on zero sleep, is just a very fast, very confused brain.
shots.scene: Race car with spinning wheels and an empty tank beside LEON slumped

shots.line: The napkin, by the way, says "check the thing." Nothing else.
shots.scene: Close-up of the napkin: 'check the thing.' with kText type

shots.line: The fix is the hardest one, because it isn't a trick. You sleep.
shots.scene: Plate THE FIX: SLEEP.; LEON in bed, moonlight

shots.line: A full night, same time every night, like medicine.
shots.scene: Bedside clock and a pill-timer on the table, LEON smiling

shots.line: Mom puts you to bed, and you can't argue, because you know she's right. You've seen the study. Problem four.
shots.scene: MOM tucks LEON in, warm lamp, he nods; label 'YOU'VE SEEN THE STUDY'

shots.line: The quiet one. You tell your best friend a joke.
shots.scene: Plate PROBLEM 4: LEON alone on a school bench at dusk, label 'THE QUIET ONE'; FRIEND sits beside him

shots.line: A good one, with four layers. He laughs at the first layer. You explain the other three. He stops laughing.
shots.scene: Two-shot on the bench: LEON tells a joke, 4 bubble layers appear (LAYER 1 to 4), FRIEND laughs at the first

shots.line: You explain why that's also funny.
shots.scene: LEON explaining a layer on a mini whiteboard, FRIEND's smile fading

shots.line: He says he has to go home.
shots.scene: FRIEND walks away off frame, LEON waves; slow pull-out

shots.line: At lunch you sit alone with a book about black holes, and a kid asks what it's about. "Everything," you say.
shots.scene: Cafeteria: LEON alone with a black-hole book, a KID asks; 'Everything,' LEON says, deadpan

shots.line: He nods politely and sits somewhere else. This part is real.
shots.scene: The kid nods politely and moves to another table; LEON alone in a wide; then cut to 1942 office

shots.line: In nineteen forty-two,
shots.scene: Sepia-cool office 1942: PSYCH writing '1942' on a board; label 1942

shots.line: the psychologist Leta Hollingworth wrote about twelve children with IQs above one hundred and eighty.
shots.scene: Twelve child silhouettes at desks, board label '12 CHILDREN · IQ 180+', one child apart from the others

shots.line: Her case studies found that kids that far ahead were hardly ever picked as leaders by their classmates,
shots.scene: Pan over the children, none of them picked as leader (a crown icon over nobody)

shots.line: and many struggled to make friends. Nobody was mean.
shots.scene: One child alone at the playground fence; label 'STRUGGLED TO MAKE FRIENDS'

shots.line: They were just on different pages of the same book.
shots.scene: Giant open book, LEON and FRIEND turning pages, FRIEND on page 1

shots.line: And you're hundreds of pages ahead. There's no clean fix.
shots.scene: LEON hundreds of pages ahead, pages flying; FRIEND tiny behind

shots.line: You learn to say smaller things.
shots.scene: LEON speaks in small word blocks, FRIEND listens

shots.line: You ask questions instead of answering them.
shots.scene: LEON asks questions, question marks drift above them

shots.line: You let your friend win at video games, and sometimes it works. Not always.
shots.scene: LEON lets FRIEND win at video games, a small sad smile at the end

shots.line: And then one winter afternoon, all of it gets tested. December.
shots.scene: Window view: winter afternoon over a pond; cold light, slow pull-out from the window

shots.line: First ice on the pond behind your house.
shots.scene: Establishing wide: the pond behind the house, first ice, LEON on the bank, label DECEMBER

shots.line: Your little sister Nia is six, and she's wearing mittens with penguins on them.
shots.scene: NIA in a yellow jacket on the shore holding the other penguin mitten up to the camera

shots.line: One of them is lying out on the ice, twenty metres from the shore. About twenty-two yards.
shots.scene: Wide: one penguin mitten lies on the ice, distance line '20 M', '≈22 YARDS'

shots.line: She steps out to get it.
shots.scene: NIA steps onto the ice, camera pushes behind LEON's shoulder

shots.line: The ice makes a sound.
shots.scene: Macro: ice surface, a fine crack starts, camera shake

shots.line: A long, low crack, like a door opening in a very big house.
shots.scene: Wide: a long crack spreads through the ice toward NIA, who freezes

shots.line: And you know exactly what that means.
shots.scene: Giant face close-up of LEON, fear, pupils widening

shots.line: The rule of thumb is to stay off until there's at least four inches of clear ice, about ten centimetres.
shots.scene: Ice cross-section with a ruler, label '4 IN ≈ 10 CM', ice thinner and cloudy

shots.line: This isn't that.
shots.scene: Cloudy ice under NIA's feet, cut between thin ice and her feet; label 'THIS ISN'T THAT'

shots.line: You can see it in the colour.
shots.scene: Close: the colour of the ice, grey-white and milky

shots.line: Your brain runs the numbers in one second, her weight, the ice, the distance, the time before the next crack.
shots.scene: LEON's head with icons orbiting: weight, ice, distance, time; one second counter

shots.line: And then rule three hits you.
shots.scene: LEON turns to his legs, lightning flash of understanding

shots.line: Your legs won't get there in time.
shots.scene: His sneakers rooted in slow motion, distance line to NIA

shots.line: And the limit hits you too. You've never seen a rescue.
shots.scene: Question mark over LEON's head, a blank diagram labelled 'RESCUE?'

shots.line: You can guess one, but a guess is not good enough.
shots.scene: LEON thinks, a guess diagram marked with a cross

shots.line: You could throw a coat, a stick, a snowball.
shots.scene: Coat, stick and snowball icons, each crossed out

shots.line: Your brain lists forty-one options in a blink, and every single one needs your arms to be faster than they are.
shots.scene: List of 41 arrows flicking by, label '41 OPTIONS', all crossed out

shots.line: So you don't run.
shots.scene: LEON freezes his legs and takes a breath, cold light

shots.line: You keep your voice calm. "Nia.
shots.scene: Close: LEON calm, palm raised toward NIA, speaks: 'Nia.'

shots.line: Stay exactly where you are. Look at me. Don't move." She freezes.
shots.scene: Two-shot: NIA looking back; LEON 'Stay exactly where you are. Look at me. Don't move.'; NIA freezes

shots.line: Then you shout the smartest thing you've ever shouted. "Help! Somebody! The pond!"
shots.scene: LEON shouts toward the houses: 'Help! Somebody! The pond!', camera pulls back

shots.line: A porch light turns on. Then another.
shots.scene: Houses at dusk: a porch light turns on, then another

shots.line: Then somebody's running with a coil of rope.
shots.scene: A silhouette runs along the fence with a coil of rope, orange jersey

shots.line: Three neighbours, all of them slower than your brain, all of them faster than your legs, and one of them has done this before.
shots.scene: Three NEIGHBORs race toward the pond; one carries the rope; wide pull-out

shots.line: You stand there with a clear head, because you ate, because you slept.
shots.scene: LEON standing calm, icons for 'ATE' and 'SLEPT' with checks beside him

shots.line: For the first time in your life, all that brainpower has one job.
shots.scene: LEON's head with all thought lines focusing into one beam toward NIA

shots.line: Know when to call people. It takes four minutes.
shots.scene: Caption 'KNOW WHEN TO CALL PEOPLE.' kText slam, then card '4 MIN'

shots.line: A rope, a firm voice, and a neighbour who knows what he's doing.
shots.scene: NEIGHBOR throws the rope, NIA grabs it, he pulls steadily

shots.line: Nia is back on the shore in a blanket, shaking, but fine.
shots.scene: NIA wrapped in a blanket on the shore, shaking, LEON sitting by her

shots.line: "I told you I'd get the mitten," she says. You look at the pond.
shots.scene: Close: NIA (talk): 'I told you I'd get the mitten.' LEON smiling with relief

shots.line: The mitten is still out there.
shots.scene: Wide: the lone penguin mitten still on the ice, far away

shots.line: It stays there until spring.
shots.scene: Time passes: the same wide, snow melts to spring, the mitten finally on grass

shots.line: Your brain solved a thousand problems this week.
shots.scene: LEON and NIA sit on the porch, thought-bubbles with equations floating away

shots.line: Your sister solved the only one she cared about, and lost the mitten.
shots.scene: NIA holds up an empty hand, LEON laughs, golden dusk light

shots.line: That night you go to bed on time.
shots.scene: LEON in bed on time, clock at 9:00 PM, soft lamp

shots.line: You're asleep in nine seconds.
shots.scene: Close: LEON asleep with 'Z' icons, nine small seconds on a timer

shots.line: The next morning, there's a note on your desk, in handwriting you don't recognise. "I saw your test."
shots.scene: Morning, a note on LEON's desk in unfamiliar handwriting; he leans in

shots.line: So who saw it, and what do they want? That's next time.
shots.scene: Close-up note: 'I saw your test.' in unfamiliar handwriting; a shadow figure by the window

shots.line: What would you do with a mind like that?
shots.scene: End screen: LEON looks to camera, question in serif italic 'What would you do with a mind like that?'

shots.line: Tell us in the comments, and subscribe, so you don't miss part two.
shots.scene: End screen: comment bubble and subscribe pill, label 'PART 2 COMING', cast lined up and fade out
